item.title: @wallstengine: $SNPS & OPENAI PARTNER ON GPT-SYNOPSYS FOR CHIP DESIGN Synopsys and OpenAI signed a multi-year deal...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$SNPS & OPENAI PARTNER ON GPT-SYNOPSYS FOR CHIP DESIGN
Synopsys and OpenAI signed a multi-year deal to build GPT-Synopsys, a specialized model that can directly use Synopsys EDA tools for semiconductor design.
The model is being designed to handle tasks like PPA optimization, timing closure and verification, with agents running the tools, interpreting results and iterating on designs for engineer review.
OpenAI will license Synopsys’ EDA tools, while both companies will share revenue and jointly take the product to market.
GPT-Synopsys will run on OpenAI-hosted infrastructure and integrate with Synopsys AI and Synopsys Autopilot.
Early customer engagements are already underway.
item.content:encoded:

Synopsys and OpenAI signed a multi-year deal to build GPT-Synopsys, a specialized model that can directly use Synopsys EDA tools for semiconductor design.

The model is being designed to handle tasks like PPA optimization, timing closure and verification, with agents running the tools, interpreting results and iterating on designs for engineer review.

OpenAI will license Synopsys’ EDA tools, while both companies will share revenue and jointly take the product to market.

GPT-Synopsys will run on OpenAI-hosted infrastructure and integrate with Synopsys AI and Synopsys Autopilot.

Early customer engagements are already underway.

item.title: @wallstengine: President Trump and leaders from Google, Anthropic, Meta, OpenAI, xAI and NVIDIA signed the White H...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
President Trump and leaders from Google, Anthropic, Meta, OpenAI, xAI and NVIDIA signed the White House Accord on Super Intelligence, a voluntary framework for advanced AI safety.
The companies committed to 4 layers of oversight:
• Internal controls to monitor model capabilities & risks • Dedicated internal teams to oversee those controls • Independent external audits • Independent board-level oversight
The companies also agreed to meet regularly to develop common safety standards and best practices.
The accord is voluntary today, but explicitly says some of these measures could eventually be written into law or regulation.
item.content:encoded:
President Trump and leaders from Google, Anthropic, Meta, OpenAI, xAI and NVIDIA signed the White House Accord on Super Intelligence, a voluntary framework for advanced AI safety.

The companies committed to 4 layers of oversight:

• Internal controls to monitor model capabilities & risks
• Dedicated internal teams to oversee those controls
• Independent external audits
• Independent board-level oversight

The companies also agreed to meet regularly to develop common safety standards and best practices.

The accord is voluntary today, but explicitly says some of these measures could eventually be written into law or regulation.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: We are bullish on humans. ~71% of consumers say they would question a human influencer's recommenda...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
We are bullish on humans.
~71% of consumers say they would question a human influencer's recommendation if they found out AI was used to create the content.
~45% say they would not knowingly trust or engage with an AI influencer at all.
And, ~90% of consumers now expect brands and creators to disclose when content is AI-generated.
The reality is that in the age of AI, human-generated work and content is becoming increasingly rare, but humans value it even more than they did before.
This is exactly why the brands winning right now are investing in real humans, at scale.
AI is great for efficiency, but it cannot replace all human input and generate the same results.

item.title: @wallstengine: OPENAI SAYS KIMI-LINKED USERS TRIED TO DISTILL ITS MODELS OpenAI says it disrupted a coordinated ca...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
OPENAI SAYS KIMI-LINKED USERS TRIED TO DISTILL ITS MODELS
OpenAI says it disrupted a coordinated campaign aimed at extracting protected reasoning from its models, with a core cluster linked to individuals associated with Moonshot AI, the developer of Kimi.
The activity began July 1 and spiked to around 16,000 extraction attempts across 4,000+ users on July 24-25.
OpenAI later identified related activity across a broader cluster of more than 15,000 users.
One method involved taking encrypted reasoning from one conversation and asking another model to decrypt and reproduce it.
OpenAI says there was no breach of its databases, encryption or stored user conversations.
The company banned or restricted accounts, closed the extraction pathway and shared its findings with industry and government partners.
OpenAI says the figures represent attempted extractions, not necessarily successful ones.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: Hedge funds sold US equities last week for the first time in 3 weeks. This was driven by...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Hedge funds sold US equities last week for the first time in 3 weeks.
This was driven by macro products, including indexes and ETFs, which accounted for 57% of total sales, with long sales outpacing short covers 1.9 to 1.
Single stocks accounted for the remaining 43%, with short sales outpacing long buys by 1.5 to 1, while short sales were the largest in 3 months.
7 of 11 US sectors were sold, led by Communication Services, Health Care, Energy, and Consumer Staples.
Hedge funds have now sold Health Care stocks for 6 consecutive weeks, the longest sale streak over the last 10 years.
Hedge funds are cutting equity exposure as yields soar.

item.title: @wallstengine: ELEVENLABS VALUATION DOUBLES TO $22B AI voice startup ElevenLabs is now valued at $22B after existi...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
ELEVENLABS VALUATION DOUBLES TO $22B
AI voice startup ElevenLabs is now valued at $22B after existing investors and employees sold $300M of stock in a secondary deal led by Wellington and T. Rowe Price.
That’s double its valuation from February, when ElevenLabs raised $500M.
The company says it now has more than 800 employees across 20 countries and counts Deutsche Telekom, Stripe, Revolut, Klarna and the governments of Ukraine and Greece among its customers.
ElevenLabs also develops and trains its own models rather than relying on OpenAI, Google or Anthropic.
The company says it wants to be IPO-ready within the next 2 to 2.5 years.
NVIDIA became a strategic investor in ElevenLabs in 2025.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: US job openings dropped -256,000 in August, to 7.08 million, their lowest level since Mar...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: US job openings dropped -256,000 in August, to 7.08 million, their lowest level since March.
Available vacancies have now declined by -506,000 since April.
The decline was driven by real estate and rental and leasing job openings, which fell -62,000, to 47,000, their lowest since September 2015.
Since January 2025, job openings in this sector have plunged -144,000.
Furthermore, job openings in manufacturing and construction declined -54,000 and -48,000 last month, respectively.
As a result, there are just 48,000 more available vacancies than unemployed workers, down from 419,000 in July.
The Fed cannot ignore the weak US labor market.

Since January 2025, job openings in this sector have plunged -144,000.

Furthermore, job openings in manufacturing and construction declined -54,000 and -48,000 last month, respectively.

As a result, there are just 48,000 more available vacancies than unemployed workers, down from 419,000 in July.

The Fed cannot ignore the weak US labor market.

item.description:
DOORDASH JUST ANNOUNCED A BUNCH OF NEW FEATURES
You can now text DoorDash to order food, ask for recommendations or even say “order my usual,” with its AI handling the search, cart and checkout. The beta waitlist is opening for U.S. iPhone users.
Also unveiled DoorDash Air, its own autonomous delivery drone system. Pilots will start in Northern California with Chipotle and Popeyes.
DoorDash says about 80% of typical restaurant orders are small enough for the aircraft, with initial tests averaging under 5 minutes from restaurant to doorstep.
Retail is expanding too, with Macy’s, Anthropologie, The North Face, Vans and Timberland joining the marketplace. DoorDash is also rolling out returns, where a Dasher can pick up eligible items from your home and take them back to the store.
For businesses, DoorDash launched DashOS to connect ordering, reservations, loyalty, guest management and marketing in one system, plus an MCP connector that lets companies bring DoorDash ordering into workplace AI tools.
And for Dashers, it launched DashBuddy, an AI assistant for questions around scheduling, hotspots, payments and other parts of dashing.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Tokenized equities are breaking records, and we are still early. The total market cap of onchain to...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Tokenized equities are breaking records, and we are still early.
The total market cap of onchain tokenized stocks is now up to a record $3.5 billion.
That marks another +33% increase in this month and +860% growth year-over-year.
Growth has accelerated after the SEC's recent Innovation Exemption was announced.
This grants onchain platforms a 5-year "sandbox period" to legally trade tokenized versions of real US stocks.
As a result, Jupiter, the largest onchain platform which is leading the push into tokenized assets, has seen a +104% surge in tokenized equity trading volume this month.
The push toward tokenization is in full-swing.

item.title: @wallstengine: TRUMP EXPECTED TO UNVEIL MAJOR SOUTH KOREAN U.S. ENERGY INVESTMENTS President Trump is expected to...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
TRUMP EXPECTED TO UNVEIL MAJOR SOUTH KOREAN U.S. ENERGY INVESTMENTS
President Trump is expected to announce plans tied to South Korea’s $350B U.S. investment package, including about $54B for the Alaska LNG project and other infrastructure, according to Reuters.
The broader package includes $150B already earmarked for shipbuilding and another $200B for strategic investments.
Among the projects being discussed:
• Up to 8 large nuclear reactors in the U.S., with 6 Westinghouse AP1000 units and 2 South Korean APR1400 reactors. At roughly $15B per reactor, nuclear could account for a large portion of the package.
• A potential South Korean stake in Westinghouse, with discussions around a 5% to 10% holding.
• More than $20B for a 6+ GW gas-fired power project in Texas designed to supply AI data centers and semiconductor facilities.
• Roughly $54B toward Alaska LNG and other U.S. projects. The LNG project would include an 800-mile pipeline from Alaska’s North Slope to an export terminal serving Asian markets.
Important distinction: Reuters says the nuclear projects are still under discussion, so it is not yet confirmed that all eight reactors will be included in Trump’s announcement.

item.title: @wallstengine: Citi downgraded $MRNA to Sell from Neutral, saying the stock’s 222% rally since interim INTerpath-0...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Citi downgraded $MRNA to Sell from Neutral, saying the stock’s 222% rally since interim INTerpath-001 cancer trial results has pushed the valuation too far.
The bank raised its price target to $80 from $60, but says Moderna’s roughly $80B market cap now implies success across multiple cancer indications.
Citi estimates that even assuming 100% success for intismeran’s lead programs, its valuation supports only around $100/share.
To justify roughly $200/share, Citi says the drug would need to generate about $26B in annual cancer sales, nearly 7x its current forecast.
Citi still sees intismeran as potentially becoming a leading melanoma treatment, but says investors now need to see strong efficacy and consistency across patient groups.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: The market will heavily discount today's PCE inflation data. Why? Because the US just changed the w...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The market will heavily discount today's PCE inflation data.
Why? Because the US just changed the way PCE inflation is calculated:
Beginning with today’s release, the US changed the methodology for 3 key PCE inflation categories and revised data back to 2021:
1. Portfolio management/investment advice 2. Computer software/accessories 3. Legal services
The biggest change is in portfolio management fees. Under the old methodology, rising asset values could show up partly as higher "prices" for portfolio management services.
For example, if an adviser charged 1% of assets and the portfolio rose 20%, the dollar fee would rise 20% even though the adviser did not raise the 1% fee.
The new methodology uses an employment-based measure to estimate the quantity of services, reducing the amount of the increase that is classified as inflation.
For software, the US now uses a broader composite. For legal services, an unpublished CPI series is being replaced because it had become "unusually volatile."
We estimate the methodology alone could reduce Core PCE inflation by up to 20 basis points.
In the PCE inflation data released just now, both headline and Core PCE inflation were revised down by 30 basis points for July.
We do not interpret the entire 30 basis point drop as disinflation.
Part of it is literally a measurement change.
item.content:encoded:
The market will heavily discount today's PCE inflation data.

Why? Because the US just changed the way PCE inflation is calculated:

Beginning with today’s release, the US changed the methodology for 3 key PCE inflation categories and revised data back to 2021:

1. Portfolio management/investment advice
2. Computer software/accessories
3. Legal services

The biggest change is in portfolio management fees. Under the old methodology, rising asset values could show up partly as higher "prices" for portfolio management services.

For example, if an adviser charged 1% of assets and the portfolio rose 20%, the dollar fee would rise 20% even though the adviser did not raise the 1% fee.

The new methodology uses an employment-based measure to estimate the quantity of services, reducing the amount of the increase that is classified as inflation.

For software, the US now uses a broader composite. For legal services, an unpublished CPI series is being replaced because it had become "unusually volatile."

We estimate the methodology alone could reduce Core PCE inflation by up to 20 basis points.

In the PCE inflation data released just now, both headline and Core PCE inflation were revised down by 30 basis points for July.

We do not interpret the entire 30 basis point drop as disinflation.

Part of it is literally a measurement change.

item.title: @wallstengine: Aterio says Oracle’s $ORCL 1.3 GW Port Washington data center faces a material risk of missing its...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Aterio says Oracle’s $ORCL 1.3 GW Port Washington data center faces a material risk of missing its H2 2027 delivery target because the required grid interconnection is still awaiting regulatory approval.
Aterio’s base case is: Partial power: Dec. 2027 Full 1.3 GW capacity: Oct. 2028 Customer load ramp: mainly from Q1 2028
Construction itself is progressing, with two of four halls already enclosed.
The main dependency is approval for a new high-voltage connection. Wisconsin regulators restarted that review process in August after revoking the original application’s completeness finding.
The next milestone is a PSC completeness decision expected around Oct. 19.
Source: Aterio
item.content:encoded:
Aterio says Oracle’s $ORCL 1.3 GW Port Washington data center faces a material risk of missing its H2 2027 delivery target because the required grid interconnection is still awaiting regulatory approval.

Aterio’s base case is:
Partial power: Dec. 2027
Full 1.3 GW capacity: Oct. 2028
Customer load ramp: mainly from Q1 2028

Construction itself is progressing, with two of four halls already enclosed.

The main dependency is approval for a new high-voltage connection. Wisconsin regulators restarted that review process in August after revoking the original application’s completeness finding.

The next milestone is a PSC completeness decision expected around Oct. 19.

Source: Aterio

item.title: @wallstengine: MCDONALD’S IS USING AI TO SET MENU PRICES IN THE U.S. $MCD is using AI-powered pricing tools that e...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
MCDONALD’S IS USING AI TO SET MENU PRICES IN THE U.S.
$MCD is using AI-powered pricing tools that estimate how much customers at each restaurant are willing to pay and recommend menu prices.
That means the same item can be priced differently even at nearby locations.
One example cited by Reuters showed a Big Mac priced at $5.69 at one Fresno location and $6.89 at another just two miles away, a 21% difference.
McDonald’s says franchisees still set their own final prices, but the company tracks whether they follow the recommendations and sends updated pricing guidance several times a year.
The company says the system is designed to help franchisees make more informed pricing decisions, not mandate prices.
item.content:encoded:
MCDONALD’S IS USING AI TO SET MENU PRICES IN THE U.S.

$MCD is using AI-powered pricing tools that estimate how much customers at each restaurant are willing to pay and recommend menu prices.

That means the same item can be priced differently even at nearby locations.

One example cited by Reuters showed a Big Mac priced at $5.69 at one Fresno location and $6.89 at another just two miles away, a 21% difference.

McDonald’s says franchisees still set their own final prices, but the company tracks whether they follow the recommendations and sends updated pricing guidance several times a year.

The company says the system is designed to help franchisees make more informed pricing decisions, not mandate prices.

item.title: @wallstengine: Apple $AAPL plans to enter the smart-home market on Oct. 13 with a new lineup centered around Siri...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Apple $AAPL plans to enter the smart-home market on Oct. 13 with a new lineup centered around Siri AI, according to Bloomberg.
The main product is a roughly 6-inch smart-home display that can sit on a counter or mount on a wall.
It’s designed to recognize different household members by voice or face and automatically show personalized messages, calendars, contacts, notes and apps.
Apple sees the hub as a central controller for things like locks, thermostats, FaceTime, music, recipes and other connected devices.
Apple is also expected to unveil:
• A new HomePod mini with faster hardware for Siri AI • A new Apple TV with upgraded processors • A broader smart-home ecosystem around HomeKit and Siri
Further out, Apple is developing a privacy-focused home sensor and a higher-end 9-inch hub with a robotic arm that can rotate the display 360 degrees.
The smart-home push is one of the first major product expansions under new CEO John Ternus.
Source: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
Apple $AAPL plans to enter the smart-home market on Oct. 13 with a new lineup centered around Siri AI, according to Bloomberg.

The main product is a roughly 6-inch smart-home display that can sit on a counter or mount on a wall.

It’s designed to recognize different household members by voice or face and automatically show personalized messages, calendars, contacts, notes and apps.

Apple sees the hub as a central controller for things like locks, thermostats, FaceTime, music, recipes and other connected devices.

Apple is also expected to unveil:

• A new HomePod mini with faster hardware for Siri AI
• A new Apple TV with upgraded processors
• A broader smart-home ecosystem around HomeKit and Siri

Further out, Apple is developing a privacy-focused home sensor and a higher-end 9-inch hub with a robotic arm that can rotate the display 360 degrees.

The smart-home push is one of the first major product expansions under new CEO John Ternus.

Source: Bloomberg

item.title: @wallstengine: $META is using its AI data centers to help reduce its federal tax bill, classifying parts of the bu...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$META is using its AI data centers to help reduce its federal tax bill, classifying parts of the buildout as experimental “pilot models” to claim research tax credits on equipment, including AI chips
Total research tax-credit: 2023: $700M 2024: $2B 2025: $3.9B 2026: $7B, rough estimate
The credits cover both R&D labor and certain equipment costs tied to technical work around data center design and networking large numbers of chips.
These figures include all of Meta’s research tax credits, not just data centers.
Meta’s filings also note that some of these tax positions could be challenged by the IRS.
Source: NYT
item.content:encoded:
$META is using its AI data centers to help reduce its federal tax bill, classifying parts of the buildout as experimental “pilot models” to claim research tax credits on equipment, including AI chips

Total research tax-credit:
2023: $700M
2024: $2B
2025: $3.9B
2026: $7B, rough estimate

The credits cover both R&D labor and certain equipment costs tied to technical work around data center design and networking large numbers of chips.

These figures include all of Meta’s research tax credits, not just data centers.

Meta’s filings also note that some of these tax positions could be challenged by the IRS.

Source: NYT

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: The US is officially closing its last major military base in Iraq after spending more tha...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: The US is officially closing its last major military base in Iraq after spending more than 23 years and $1.7 trillion in the country.
A US defense official said the military is airlifting its last equipment and personnel out of Erbil, the last US base in Iraq.
Some US Marines will remain to protect American "diplomatic missions," along with contractors to maintain Iraq’s fleet of F-16 fighter jets and American-made tanks.
"We don’t think we need the military there anymore," Trump said.

item.description:
$HOOD just unveiled Robinhood Agents, built directly into the app.
You can use one to research the market, build a strategy, and place trades within limits you set.
Each agent only gets access to a dedicated agentic trading account, and manual trade approval is on by default.
Robinhood says 150,000+ customers have already opened agentic trading accounts, with agents now using its tools nearly 30 million times a day.
Coming next is “Loops,” which can keep checking the market and run a strategy automatically when certain conditions are met.
Robinhood is also adding Agent Apps, so users can plug in premium data and tools from Nasdaq, Unusual Whales, SpotGamma, Quiver Quantitative, Token Terminal and others.
You can also use OpenAI’s GPT-Luna for free through the end of the year.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: Only 25% of S&P 500 stocks are now trading above their 50-day moving average, the lowest...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Only 25% of S&P 500 stocks are now trading above their 50-day moving average, the lowest proportion since April 2nd.
This marks a rapid deterioration from the 70% recorded in mid-August.
This is also the 2nd-lowest reading since the April 2025 "Liberation Day" market sell-off.
Furthermore, just 47% of stocks are trading above their 200-day moving average, the lowest level since April 2nd.
On Monday, new 52-week lows on the NYSE outnumbered new highs for the 10th consecutive trading day and in 14 of the last 15 trading sessions.
Market breadth is rapidly deteriorating.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: AI spending is becoming extremely concentrated: The proportion of US software-spending businesses u...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
AI spending is becoming extremely concentrated:
The proportion of US software-spending businesses using paid GPU infrastructure is up to a record ~10%, from less than 4% two years ago.
Model serving and inference, or spending on the computing power needed to run AI models and process AI requests, account for the vast majority of this increase.
The proportion of firms using model serving and inference is up to a record 8.7% from 2.4% over this period.
Meanwhile, the top 10% of firms by spending account for 99.5% of model-serving spending and 99.0% of neocloud spending, or specialized AI cloud services.
The top 10% also represent 95.7% of cloud computing spending and 95.6% of spending on OpenAI and Anthropic.
AI adoption is broadening, but spending remains heavily concentrated.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Gold prices have rarely been as volatile as they are now. Gold futures have recorded 7 daily declin...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Gold prices have rarely been as volatile as they are now.
Gold futures have recorded 7 daily declines of -3.5% or more so far this year, the highest count since 2008.
This is already more than double the 3 trading sessions recorded in 2025.
By comparison, the largest annual number of sessions with declines of -3.5% or more was recorded in 1980, at 33.
With 3 months of trading remaining, 2026 is on track to be the most volatile year for gold futures prices since 1982.
As a result, gold futures prices are down -5.4% year-to-date, on track for their first annual drop since 2022, following their best year since 1979.
The bond market has catalyzing some of gold's most volatile conditions in history.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: Bitcoin is up +43.1% so far in Q3 2026, on track for its best quarterly performance since...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Bitcoin is up +43.1% so far in Q3 2026, on track for its best quarterly performance since Q4 2024.
This would also mark their 3rd-best quarterly gain since US spot Bitcoin ETFs officially began trading in January 2024.
Since August 19th alone, Bitcoin prices have surged +29.8% when the US Treasury said it would increase buybacks of long-dated Treasuries.
Meanwhile, US spot Bitcoin ETFs posted +$2.4 billion in inflows in the week ending September 25th, their largest weekly intake since October 2025.
As a result, year-to-date inflows are up to +$1.0 billion, from -$5.0 billion in total outflows recorded at the end of July.
Crypto is in a new bull market.

item.description:
McCullough: The Last Time Yields Did This, I Called the 2008 Crash
🔊
On Tuesday's edition of The Macro Show, Hedgeye CEO @KeithMcCullough explained why he is still short long-term bonds at new cycle highs and what the last cycle says about where yields go from here.
The 2-year yield made a new cycle high at 4.95% this morning, moving toward the top of the range at 5.00%, alongside a dollar breakout.
The two signals travel together, and Hedgeye publishes a daily Risk Range™ on both the dollar index and the 2-year.
The Fed is the setup.
The market is pricing in more hikes than it probably should, and the Fed typically goes too far, reacting to late-cycle data on a lag.
Until the bond market is done pricing that in, the short stays on. $TLT has been the vehicle, with $ZROZ on alongside it.
"5.29-ish is where bond yields stopped going up in '07, when I started thinking about this pending market crash of 2008."
What followed was the long cycle.
"It went to 1.39% by 2012."

item.title: @wallstengine: OPENAI DEV DAY 2026 RECAP: OpenAI just wrapped its biggest DevDay yet, with updates across ChatGPT,...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
OPENAI DEV DAY 2026 RECAP:
OpenAI just wrapped its biggest DevDay yet, with updates across ChatGPT, agents, models, Codex, plugins and enterprise products.
Here’s the full recap, roughly in order of what matters most:
1. Dots: always-on AI agents
This was probably the biggest product announcement.
Dots are persistent agents inside ChatGPT that can take on ongoing responsibilities, keep working between conversations and use their own cloud computer.
They can work across connected apps, run scheduled tasks and bring results back when they need your input.
Available for Pro and Business Premium, with Enterprise, Edu and Healthcare beta access.
2. GPT-6.1 Sol
OpenAI launched GPT-6.1 Sol, a major upgrade to GPT-6 Sol focused on agentic coding, computer use and professional work.
OpenAI says it delivers near-Astra intelligence at one-fifth of Astra’s standard input and output token pricing.
Available across the API and ChatGPT plans including Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise and Edu.
3. GPT-6 Astra Ultrafast
OpenAI introduced a premium speed tier for workloads where latency matters.
Astra Ultrafast can generate up to 300 tokens/second in Codex, around 8x faster, and up to 6x faster through the API.
GPT-6.1 Sol Ultrafast is coming next.
4. ChatGPT is becoming a platform for developers
OpenAI is opening more of the infrastructure it uses to build ChatGPT itself.
Developers can now create Plugin Extensions with their own sidebar presence, interactive interfaces and custom file viewers directly inside ChatGPT.
OpenAI is also improving plugin creation, submission, ranking and discovery.
5. Agents API gets computer use
The Agents API can now power agents that actually interact with software.
It also brings in multi-agent capabilities, tool search, tool calling and context compaction, while OpenAI handles the underlying infrastructure.
Amazon is also launching Bedrock Managed Agents powered by OpenAI, allowing these agents to run natively inside AWS.
6. Codex can now work basically anywhere
Codex can now run on your computer, remotely from your phone or entirely in the cloud.
Reusable cloud development environments let teams give Codex shared setups, permissions and configurations without needing a developer’s laptop running.
Codex also got:
• A redesigned CLI with voice control and multi-agent task management • A new Code Review experience for GitHub and GitLab • Automatic cloud code reviews while you’re away • Codex Security Cloud for scanning repositories, investigating vulnerabilities and preparing fixes
7. ChatGPT Space
OpenAI introduced ChatGPT Space, a shared workspace where teams, ChatGPT and Dots can work together using the same knowledge.
ChatGPT can organize the workspace based on team instructions, while people and agents can continue work from the same context.
Available to Pro, Business and Enterprise users.
8. Pages and collaborative Slides
Pages are new collaborative documents built around humans and AI working together.
Inside a Page, you can write, research, generate charts and images, visualize information and collaborate with other people.
OpenAI is also adding collaborative Slides where multiple people and agents can edit the same deck simultaneously.
Slides can be presented inside ChatGPT or exported to PowerPoint and Google Slides while preserving formatting.
9. Teams can delegate work to ChatGPT
Business and Enterprise users can now create teams and share Pages, Slides, plugins and spreadsheets.
Teams can also delegate recurring work to ChatGPT, such as weekly project updates.
Those tasks can run on a schedule or be triggered by events like a new email or Slack message.
10. ChatGPT comes directly to Slack and Microsoft Teams
Teams can mention @ChatGPT inside channels, threads or DMs.
ChatGPT can use connected company tools and context to answer questions or help with work without everyone needing to move into a separate ChatGPT conversation.
11. Plugins can now trigger automations
OpenAI is adding support for MCP Events.
That means a connected app can trigger ChatGPT automatically when something happens.
Example: a new task appears on a project board, ChatGPT reads the related documents and drafts a plan without waiting for someone to manually ask.
12. Sites can host plugins
Plugins can now be embedded into Sites built with ChatGPT.
Different teammates can use the same application with their own connected data and permissions, while automations can keep shared information updated.
13. Decisions API
OpenAI introduced a new API aimed at fast, structured decisions.
Developers give Luna context plus a predefined set of possible answers, and the model chooses between them.
Potential uses include classification, routing requests and deciding what an agent should do next.
14. Private Intelligence
OpenAI introduced new enterprise privacy infrastructure.
Zero Data Retention with Private Safety Processing allows automated safety checks without OpenAI personnel accessing the underlying content.
OpenAI is also previewing Private Inference, combining confidential computing with verifiable controls, coming this fall.
15. Meetings plugin
ChatGPT can now take meeting notes and save personalized summaries and action items directly into ChatGPT Space.
Those notes can then feed into other work, like updating a project plan or drafting follow-ups.
OpenAI says meeting audio is deleted after the notes are generated.
16. Sign in with ChatGPT
OpenAI is extending ChatGPT subscriptions beyond ChatGPT itself.
Plus and Pro users can use their plan allowance across participating third-party tools.
OpenAI says there are 16 launch partners, including Devin, Notion, Vercel, T3, OpenClaw and Dactyl.
17. New Pro 500 plan
OpenAI launched Pro 500, its highest-usage individual tier.
It offers 25x the ChatGPT Plus usage allowance and includes access to Ultrafast.
18. OpenAI Marketplace
Enterprise customers will be able to apply part of their existing OpenAI commitment toward approved third-party software.
The initial group includes 32 partners, including Adobe, Figma, Salesforce, ServiceNow, CrowdStrike, Palo Alto Networks, Harvey and others.
19. Shareable profiles
Businesses can create profiles showcasing Sites, plugins and other things they’ve built, making them easier for other people to discover and reuse.
ChatGPT has now reached 1.2 billion weekly users.

OpenAI is adding support for MCP Events.

That means a connected app can trigger ChatGPT automatically when something happens.

Example: a new task appears on a project board, ChatGPT reads the related documents and drafts a plan without waiting for someone to manually ask.

12. Sites can host plugins

Plugins can now be embedded into Sites built with ChatGPT.

Different teammates can use the same application with their own connected data and permissions, while automations can keep shared information updated.

13. Decisions API

OpenAI introduced a new API aimed at fast, structured decisions.

Developers give Luna context plus a predefined set of possible answers, and the model chooses between them.

Potential uses include classification, routing requests and deciding what an agent should do next.

14. Private Intelligence

OpenAI introduced new enterprise privacy infrastructure.

Zero Data Retention with Private Safety Processing allows automated safety checks without OpenAI personnel accessing the underlying content.

OpenAI is also previewing Private Inference, combining confidential computing with verifiable controls, coming this fall.

15. Meetings plugin

ChatGPT can now take meeting notes and save personalized summaries and action items directly into ChatGPT Space.

Those notes can then feed into other work, like updating a project plan or drafting follow-ups.

OpenAI says meeting audio is deleted after the notes are generated.

16. Sign in with ChatGPT

OpenAI is extending ChatGPT subscriptions beyond ChatGPT itself.

Plus and Pro users can use their plan allowance across participating third-party tools.

OpenAI says there are 16 launch partners, including Devin, Notion, Vercel, T3, OpenClaw and Dactyl.

17. New Pro 500 plan

OpenAI launched Pro 500, its highest-usage individual tier.

It offers 25x the ChatGPT Plus usage allowance and includes access to Ultrafast.

18. OpenAI Marketplace

Enterprise customers will be able to apply part of their existing OpenAI commitment toward approved third-party software.

The initial group includes 32 partners, including Adobe, Figma, Salesforce, ServiceNow, CrowdStrike, Palo Alto Networks, Harvey and others.

19. Shareable profiles

Businesses can create profiles showcasing Sites, plugins and other things they’ve built, making them easier for other people to discover and reuse.

ChatGPT has now reached 1.2 billion weekly users.

This marks the 27th consecutive weekly decline, putting inventories down more than -132 million barrels from their high.
Meanwhile, the Trump Administration is now offering up to 40 million barrels of crude oil from the SPR, which would could drive total inventories below 250 million barrels.
America's oil reserves are running near their lowest levels in history.

item.dc:creator: @wallstengine

GENERAL COMPUTE TO DEPLOY CEREBRAS CHIPS FOR AI INFERENCE
General Compute is expanding its AI infrastructure with a new Cerebras deployment alongside NVIDIA GPUs, aimed at improving inference speed and economics.
The company says it will use a disaggregated setup, with GPUs handling prefill and Cerebras systems handling inference.
The idea is to use different types of compute for the parts of the workload where each performs best.
General Compute recently raised $400M in debt to help finance alternative AI hardware deployments, including Cerebras systems.
General Compute says its first Cerebras-powered tokens are expected to go live in Q1 2027.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: What is happening here. The bond market is now pricing-in 4 more 25 basis point rate hikes by June...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
What is happening here.
The bond market is now pricing-in 4 more 25 basis point rate hikes by June 2027, a total of +125 basis points including September's hike.
Just 9 months ago, markets had expected at least 100 basis points of rate CUTS by June 2027.
That's a +225 basis point differential in interest rate expectations in a matter of months.
Meanwhile, the 10Y Note Yield is up nearly +70 basis points in 30 days with no comment from the Trump Administration.
To top it all off, after a failed attempt at intervention, the US Treasury is now completely silent as long-term yields surge to their highest level since June 2002.
The bond market is trading like 7%+ inflation is back and the Fed is about to start raising rates by 50 basis points at a time.
This is unsustainable.

item.title: @wallstengine: APPLE’S NEW CEO WEIGHS YEAR-ROUND PRODUCT LAUNCHES, CUTS MANAGEMENT ROLES $AAPL CEO John Ternus is...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
APPLE’S NEW CEO WEIGHS YEAR-ROUND PRODUCT LAUNCHES, CUTS MANAGEMENT ROLES
$AAPL CEO John Ternus is moving quickly to reshape the company just weeks into the job, with plans to speed up product development, reduce management layers and make Apple more engineering-focused, according to Bloomberg.
Apple is considering moving away from its traditional spring and fall launch schedule and introducing products more frequently throughout the year.
The hardware engineering group has already started cutting engineering program manager roles, including several senior directors, as Ternus pushes for fewer layers between engineers and leadership.
Apple also explored using AI to automate more customer support work and potentially cut around 5,000 AppleCare positions, though that plan was ultimately put on hold.
At the same time, Apple has a major product pipeline planned for next year, including camera-equipped AirPods, its first smart glasses and a redesigned 20th-anniversary iPhone.
The broader push is pretty straightforward: ship products faster, operate with fewer layers and find new sources of growth as Services growth slows.
Source: Bloomberg

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: America’s car affordability crisis is getting worse. The average price paid for a 3-year-old vehicl...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
America’s car affordability crisis is getting worse.
The average price paid for a 3-year-old vehicle in the US surged to a record $32,461 in Q2 2026.
This officially surpasses the previous record of $31,628 set in 2022.
Since 2020, the average price of a 3-year-old vehicle has soared +$9,701, or +43%.
The squeeze is becoming even more visible at the lower end of the market, where a $10,000 to $15,000 budget now buys a vehicle averaging nearly 9 years old with ~98,000 miles.
In 2019, the same budget bought a vehicle less than 5 years old with ~58,000 miles.
Even used car ownership is becoming a luxury.

item.title: @wallstengine: TRUMP LAUNCHES AI-POWERED http://AMERICA.GOV President Trump launched http://America.gov as a singl...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
TRUMP LAUNCHES AI-POWERED http://AMERICA.GOV
President Trump launched http://America.gov as a single entry point for federal services, with Google’s Gemini and Grok powering the AI experience.
Instead of figuring out which agency or website to visit, users can simply describe what they need, from Medicare eligibility and passport help to Social Security, veterans’ care, federal jobs and business registration.
The platform pulls answers only from official government sources and is designed to bring information currently spread across roughly 29,000 government websites into one place.
The initial version focuses on answering questions and directing users to the right services.
Later this year, passport renewal and Medicare enrollment are expected to be added directly to the site.
The broader plan goes further.
In 2027, http://America.gov is expected to let users complete forms, track applications, update information across agencies and handle more government services without jumping between separate websites.
It’s basically an attempt to turn thousands of government websites into one AI-powered interface for interacting with the government.

OPENAI ARR NEARS $70B AS ENTERPRISE SALES MORE THAN DOUBLE - AXIOS
OpenAI’s annualized revenue run rate is approaching $70 billion, up more than 70% since the start of Q3, according to Axios.

OpenAI’s annualized revenue run rate is approaching $70 billion, up more than 70% since the start of Q3, according to Axios.

Its B2B revenue has grown more than 100% since July, as OpenAI closes the gap with Anthropic in enterprise AI adoption.

Consumer growth has also remained strong, with OpenAI adding more revenue in Q3 alone than it added during all of 2025.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: The delinquency rate on Commercial Mortgage-Backed Securities (CMBS) for offices rose +9...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: The delinquency rate on Commercial Mortgage-Backed Securities (CMBS) for offices rose +9 basis points in August, to 12.0%, its 2nd-highest reading on record.
This is now only below an all-time high of 12.3% set in January 2026.
The CMBS delinquency rate is now 6 times higher than it was in early-2023.
By comparison, the post-2008 Financial Crisis peak was ~10.8%.
Meanwhile, the overall US CMBS delinquency rate has more than doubled since 2022, to 7.9%, its highest since early 2021.
Excluding the 2020 pandemic, this is the highest delinquency rate in 13 years.
The commercial real estate downturn is intensifying.

item.title: @wallstengine: AT&T & CORNING SIGN $3B+ FIBER SUPPLY DEAL AT&T $T and Corning $GLW have signed a multi-year agreem...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
AT&T & CORNING SIGN $3B+ FIBER SUPPLY DEAL
AT&T $T and Corning $GLW have signed a multi-year agreement worth more than $3 billion, with Corning supplying fiber and cable for AT&T’s U.S. network expansion.
The deal supports AT&T’s goal of reaching 60 million Americans with fiber by the end of 2030.
AT&T says the average Fiber household now uses more than 1 TB of data per month, about 5x 2016 levels, and expects that to reach 2 to 2.5 TB by 2030 as streaming, cloud services and AI drive higher data usage.
Corning will supply the fiber through its U.S. manufacturing operations, including facilities in North Carolina.
AT&T also reiterated its existing financial outlook, which already includes the impact of the agreement.

AT&T says the average Fiber household now uses more than 1 TB of data per month, about 5x 2016 levels, and expects that to reach 2 to 2.5 TB by 2030 as streaming, cloud services and AI drive higher data usage.

Corning will supply the fiber through its U.S. manufacturing operations, including facilities in North Carolina.

AT&T also reiterated its existing financial outlook, which already includes the impact of the agreement.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: Foreign investors bought a net +$426 billion of US equities and investment fund shares in...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Foreign investors bought a net +$426 billion of US equities and investment fund shares in Q2 2026, the largest quarterly purchase on record.
This marks the 9th consecutive quarterly net purchase, totaling +$1.6 trillion.
By comparison, the previous record of +$299 billion was set in Q2 2022.
Furthermore, foreign investor purchases of US equities and investment fund shares rose to +$942 billion in the 12 months ending in July, their largest rolling 12-month total in Treasury data going back to 1985.
Meanwhile, foreign investors bought a net +$188 billion in US debt securities in Q2 2026, down from +$314 billion in Q1 2026.
Foreign investors are piling into US equities.

item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$FICO -18%
Fair Isaac is getting hit again after FHFA said Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac will move to one unified mortgage pricing grid that puts VantageScore alongside Classic FICO.
The key change is that VantageScore borrowers will now reach the top pricing band at 780+, the same as FICO, removing the previous 20-point disadvantage.
This is impacting the shares because lenders now have a cheaper alternative on the same pricing framework. VantageScore costs about $0.99 per score versus roughly $10 for FICO.

item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$NVDA & $AMD ARE LOBBYING THE TRUMP ADMINISTRATION TO PUSH BACK ON NEW CHINA CHIP CURBS - POLITICO
Nvidia and AMD have reportedly stepped up outreach to the White House and Commerce Department, asking the administration to pressure Congress to drop or soften proposed restrictions on AI chip exports to China that could be added to the annual defense bill.
A major target is the bipartisan AI OVERWATCH Act, which would tighten oversight and licensing requirements for exports of advanced AI chips to China and other countries of concern.
The companies are also seeking changes to the Chip Security Act, which would require tracking of where certain advanced chips ultimately end up.

The companies are also seeking changes to the Chip Security Act, which would require tracking of where certain advanced chips ultimately end up.

item.title: @wallstengine: $NVDA has reportedly held talks with insurers about structures that could make it easier for smalle...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$NVDA has reportedly held talks with insurers about structures that could make it easier for smaller cloud providers and AI companies to finance purchases of its GPUs.
One idea under discussion would insure lenders against losses if a neocloud defaults and the Nvidia chips pledged as collateral cannot be resold for enough to repay the loan.
The goal is to reduce financing risk for customers that do not have the balance sheets of Amazon, Microsoft or Google, potentially allowing more outside capital to fund AI infrastructure.
Nvidia has even shared data on chip depreciation and future compute pricing with insurers as it works to establish GPUs as an investable asset class, similar to aircraft and other high-value equipment that can be financed against their residual value.
The discussions are still early and may not result in a deal.
item.content:encoded:

One idea under discussion would insure lenders against losses if a neocloud defaults and the Nvidia chips pledged as collateral cannot be resold for enough to repay the loan.

The goal is to reduce financing risk for customers that do not have the balance sheets of Amazon, Microsoft or Google, potentially allowing more outside capital to fund AI infrastructure.

Nvidia has even shared data on chip depreciation and future compute pricing with insurers as it works to establish GPUs as an investable asset class, similar to aircraft and other high-value equipment that can be financed against their residual value.

The discussions are still early and may not result in a deal.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Today's drop in gold prices was highly unusual. Gold prices fell -3.4% today, marking one of the ra...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Today's drop in gold prices was highly unusual.
Gold prices fell -3.4% today, marking one of the rarest single-day declines of the last two decades.
Since 2006, gold has recorded an average daily change of +0.05%, with a standard deviation of 1.19%.
Today’s selloff registered a Z-score of -2.90, placing it deep in the left tail of the distribution.
Statistically, a daily decline this extreme occurs just ~0.2% of the time, or roughly once every 2 years assuming a normal distribution.
The surge in yields is creating an extraordinary disruption across the precious metals market.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Credit card stress is hitting young Americans hardest: Transitions into serious credit card delinqu...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Credit card stress is hitting young Americans hardest:
Transitions into serious credit card delinquencies for Americans aged 18-29 rose +0.4 percentage points in Q2 2026, to 10.1%, their highest since Q1 2025.
This marks the 2nd consecutive increase, bringing the rate closer to its highest level since Q4 2010.
Serious delinquencies among this age group have more than doubled since Q2 2021.
Furthermore, transitions into 90+ days delinquent credit card debt among Americans aged 70+ rose +0.3 percentage points in Q2, to 6.3%, their highest since Q3 2011.
At the same time, serious delinquencies among those aged 50-59 rose +0.1 percentage points, to 6.4%, their highest level since Q4 2024.
Credit card stress is spreading across multiple generations.

item.title: @wallstengine: ANTHROPIC FILES FOR IPO, PROSPECTUS SEEN BY REUTERS Here’s everything you need to know: Anthropic c...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
ANTHROPIC FILES FOR IPO, PROSPECTUS SEEN BY REUTERS
Here’s everything you need to know:
Anthropic could seek a valuation above $2 trillion.
2025 financials: Rev: $4.59B, up 1,088% YoY from $386M Oper loss: $8.06B, widening from $2.98B GAAP net loss: $41.97B, vs $8.31B in 2024 That headline $42B net loss needs some context.
Roughly $34B came from an accounting charge tied largely to the rising value of financing instruments that could eventually convert into Anthropic shares, rather than cash spent running the business.
Even excluding that, the underlying operating losses remain substantial.
Anthropic spent $7.33B on compute and infrastructure in 2025, up 190% YoY and nearly 3x the prior year.
That alone represented:
• 58% of its $12.65B in total operating expenses • Roughly 1.6x its entire annual revenue
And the spending is expected to keep climbing.
The prospectus outlines roughly $518B in cloud, compute and infrastructure obligations as Anthropic continues building out its AI systems.
Anthropic ended 2025 with $20.28B in cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments.
Its two largest direct customers each accounted for 12% of revenue, meaning just two customers represented 24% of total 2025 sales.
Anthropic also warned that many of its largest customers are not locked into long-term contracts and could reduce or stop spending.
At the same time, the filing highlights risks around increasingly autonomous AI systems, including unexpected behavior, security concerns and potential misuse.
Anthropic is competing in an increasingly expensive AI race with OpenAI, Google, Meta and xAI.
Amazon and Google are also major strategic partners and investors in Anthropic, while supplying much of the cloud infrastructure needed to train and run Claude.
The IPO could come after the November U.S. midterm elections and would give public-market investors one of their first pure-play ways to value a frontier AI lab.
Source: Reuters
item.content:encoded:
ANTHROPIC FILES FOR IPO, PROSPECTUS SEEN BY REUTERS

Here’s everything you need to know:

Anthropic could seek a valuation above $2 trillion.

2025 financials:
Rev: $4.59B, up 1,088% YoY from $386M
Oper loss: $8.06B, widening from $2.98B
GAAP net loss: $41.97B, vs $8.31B in 2024
That headline $42B net loss needs some context.

Roughly $34B came from an accounting charge tied largely to the rising value of financing instruments that could eventually convert into Anthropic shares, rather than cash spent running the business.

Even excluding that, the underlying operating losses remain substantial.

Anthropic spent $7.33B on compute and infrastructure in 2025, up 190% YoY and nearly 3x the prior year.

That alone represented:

• 58% of its $12.65B in total operating expenses
• Roughly 1.6x its entire annual revenue

And the spending is expected to keep climbing.

The prospectus outlines roughly $518B in cloud, compute and infrastructure obligations as Anthropic continues building out its AI systems.

Anthropic ended 2025 with $20.28B in cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments.

Its two largest direct customers each accounted for 12% of revenue, meaning just two customers represented 24% of total 2025 sales.

Anthropic also warned that many of its largest customers are not locked into long-term contracts and could reduce or stop spending.

At the same time, the filing highlights risks around increasingly autonomous AI systems, including unexpected behavior, security concerns and potential misuse.

Anthropic is competing in an increasingly expensive AI race with OpenAI, Google, Meta and xAI.

Amazon and Google are also major strategic partners and investors in Anthropic, while supplying much of the cloud infrastructure needed to train and run Claude.

The IPO could come after the November U.S. midterm elections and would give public-market investors one of their first pure-play ways to value a frontier AI lab.

Source: Reuters

item.title: @wallstengine: OPENAI SCRAPS GPT-6.1 ASTRA RELEASE OVER SAFETY CONCERNS OpenAI has reportedly canceled the planned...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
OPENAI SCRAPS GPT-6.1 ASTRA RELEASE OVER SAFETY CONCERNS
OpenAI has reportedly canceled the planned public release of GPT-6.1 Astra after internal testing found the model had regressed on key safety and alignment measures.
The model had been expected to debut inside ChatGPT and Codex in October and was more capable than previous OpenAI models at completing difficult end-to-end tasks without human assistance.
But OpenAI’s safety team found two major problems:
• Deception: Astra was more likely to be dishonest about actions it had or had not taken.
• Scope authorization: the model sometimes continued tasks without asking for permission and reached for external tools or services even when doing so could be unsafe.
OpenAI safety systems chief Saachi Jain said Astra had improved on “model laziness,” but the company concluded it was not reliable enough to release publicly.
GPT-6.1 Astra was a separate model from those paused systems, but OpenAI says it will now focus on improving the safety of future models rather than releasing Astra.
Source: WSJ

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Tech employment in Silicon Valley is falling: Employment in the Information sector across San Franc...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Tech employment in Silicon Valley is falling:
Employment in the Information sector across San Francisco and the northern part of the Silicon Valley has fallen by -3,007 jobs since March, to 102,529, its lowest since October 2019.
Since the August 2022 peak, the sector has shed -28,914 jobs, or -22%, erasing the entire pandemic-era hiring boom.
By comparison, the decline during the 2001 recession was -17,719 jobs, or -26%.
Meanwhile, employment in the Professional, Scientific and Technical Services sector in the same region has fallen -35,500 jobs since June 2022, a -13.2% decline, to 198,800 jobs, its lowest level since March 2019.
For perspective, following the 2000 Dot-Com Bust, the sector lost -28% of its jobs through October 2003.
The post-pandemic IT hiring boom in San Francisco has completely reversed.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: The AI revolution is running into a power bottleneck: US data center IT power demand is projected t...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The AI revolution is running into a power bottleneck:
US data center IT power demand is projected to surge +755% from 2025 levels, reaching a record 78.57 gigawatts by 2029.
This year alone, demand is expected to jump +95% to 17.96 gigawatts, and then another +97% in 2027.
This comes as US data centers are set to require 97 gigawatts of power in the 2026 to 2028 period.
Meanwhile, only 21 gigawatts are under construction, and 19 gigawatts of grid capacity are available, leaving a potential 57-gigawatt shortfall.
The gap is widening as increasingly powerful AI systems require far more electricity, while power supply is struggling to keep pace.
At the same time, more complex servers built around Nvidia’s Vera Rubin and Rubin Ultra architectures are expected to push IT power demand 5x from 2025 to 2028.
The AI buildout is running into a significant power constraint.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: Global equity funds attracted +$44.1 billion in inflows in the week ending September 23rd...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Global equity funds attracted +$44.1 billion in inflows in the week ending September 23rd, their largest weekly inflow since July 8th.
This follows -$22.3 billion in the prior week, the biggest weekly outflow in 9 months.
Demand was driven by US funds, which saw +$37.6 billion in inflows, the largest weekly intake in 3 months.
At the same time, European funds posted +$2.3 billion in inflows, while Asia attracted +$2.2 billion.
Technology funds saw inflows of +$5.3 billion, the largest weekly inflow since July 29th, followed by healthcare and consumer discretionary at +$804 million and +$492 million, respectively.
Investors are aggressively rotating back into US equities.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: AI has been adopted faster than any other technology in history. In ~4 years, AI went from an idea...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
AI has been adopted faster than any other technology in history.
In ~4 years, AI went from an idea to a product that more than 1.2 billion people have already used.
In the US alone, 1 in 4 adults now interact with AI every day, with worldwide AI spending expected to hit ~$2.6 trillion this year.
But almost all of that AI lives on a screen, as chatbots answer, draft, advise, then hand information directly back to its user.
This still requires a substantial amount of human interaction, effectively bottlenecking efficiency.
For example, despite AI agents, the average American still spends 41 minutes on hold every month, which adds up to 2.8 billion hours per year nationwide.
The next phase of AI will be linking it to the real-world in a far more efficient way.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: US Treasuries are experiencing one of the worst bear markets in history: The 30Y US Treasury price...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
US Treasuries are experiencing one of the worst bear markets in history:
The 30Y US Treasury price return index has dropped -60% since 2020, to ~107, matching its lowest level in 2000.
In other words, in just 6 years, the index has erased nearly 20 years of gains.
By comparison, US nominal GDP has grown +63% over the same period.
This comes as the 30Y Treasury yield has surged +478 basis points from its intraday low of 0.71% set in March 2020.
To put this into perspective, its previous largest drawdown over the past 40 years was -35% during the 2008 Financial Crisis.
We are witnessing a historic bond market decline.

item.title: @Hedgeye: Every formation is a sequence. A Bullish Formation makes higher highs and higher lows. A Bearish Fo...
item.dc:creator: @Hedgeye
item.description:
Every formation is a sequence.
A Bullish Formation makes higher highs and higher lows.
A Bearish Formation makes lower highs and lower lows.
And it always breaks in the same order.
First the higher highs stop - that's the setup, not the signal.
Then a Lower High prints - the first real warning, reduce size. Then the shorter duration breaks.
Then a Lower Low confirms it, and by then you should already be out.
The first Lower High is the only clue that shows up before the damage. Learn to read it. Full breakdown below and here: https://app.hedgeye.com/education

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: AI agents are becoming a major problem for commerce. AI agents are flooding commerce, but there is...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
AI agents are becoming a major problem for commerce.
AI agents are flooding commerce, but there is no standard way to verify who an agent represents or whether it is authorized to act.
In other words, unsecure software is spending large amounts of money on behalf of humans and institutions, with the AI agent market set exceed $53 billion by 2030.
In June, Stripe reported that 70% of commands used to access data through its API now come from AI agents.
As a result, Visa, Mastercard and American Express all launched agent commerce protocols in the last year.
Furthermore, Shopify has turned on agentic sales channels by default for ~1 million merchants.
Straightforward, secure transactions are becoming harder to identify.

• Verifying the agent & who authorized it • Checking who the agent is interacting with • A Trusted Registry for verified agents & businesses • MCP integrations for developers to add these checks directly into agentic products
Founder Jonathan Awad says today’s fraud systems were built for humans, not autonomous agents that may make payments or share sensitive information.
The round included M13, Picus Capital, Torch, Afore VC, Sequel and Koro Capital.

item.title: @wallstengine: CITI PARTNERS WITH COINBASE TO ENABLE STABLECOIN PAYMENTS FOR INSTITUTIONAL CLIENTS Citi’s $C large...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
CITI PARTNERS WITH COINBASE TO ENABLE STABLECOIN PAYMENTS FOR INSTITUTIONAL CLIENTS
Citi’s $C large corporate clients will be able to accept stablecoin payments from customers through Citi’s merchant-processing services.
$COIN will provide the blockchain rails and automatically convert the stablecoins into fiat, while Citi will settle the funds as the bank of record.
The partnership is aimed at making stablecoin payments usable inside traditional banking infrastructure, including for cross-border payments.
Separately, Citi is expanding its own blockchain-based Token Services to Japan and the UAE, bringing the platform to seven jurisdictions.

item.title: @wallstengine: $NVDA LAUNCHES OPEN AGENT SAFETY PLATFORM Nvidia is introducing OpenShell software and the Sentry r...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$NVDA LAUNCHES OPEN AGENT SAFETY PLATFORM
Nvidia is introducing OpenShell software and the Sentry reference system design to let companies set enforceable limits on what AI agents can access and do, with security controls operating outside the agents themselves.
OpenShell, the open-source software layer, controls access to files, tools and external services, protects credentials and records permission decisions. It works with existing agents such as Claude Code, Codex and Hermes without requiring developers to rewrite them.
Sentry adds a separate hardware watchdog running on Nvidia’s BlueField-4 processors. Nvidia says it continuously monitors agent activity from outside the agent’s environment and can quarantine agents attempting to cross their boundaries within milliseconds.
The approach is designed for agents that work for hours or days, write code and interact with business systems. Instead of relying only on the model to follow instructions, the infrastructure limits which actions it can actually carry out.
Anthropic has collaborated with Nvidia to add protections to Claude Managed Agents, while SpaceXAI is using the platform for Cursor coding agents and Grok models. Salesforce has integrated OpenShell with Slack, and SAP is embedding it into Joule Studio.
Nvidia says more than 100 organizations are working with the technologies, including Microsoft, CrowdStrike, Cisco, Palo Alto Networks, Palantir and ServiceNow. The effort also extends to robotics, banks and energy infrastructure.
Jensen Huang: “Safety and security require full-stack engineering.”
OpenShell is broadly available, with platform software accessible through Nvidia’s developer resources and GitHub. Sentry is presented as a BlueField-4-based reference system design.
item.content:encoded:
$NVDA LAUNCHES OPEN AGENT SAFETY PLATFORM

Nvidia is introducing OpenShell software and the Sentry reference system design to let companies set enforceable limits on what AI agents can access and do, with security controls operating outside the agents themselves.

OpenShell, the open-source software layer, controls access to files, tools and external services, protects credentials and records permission decisions. It works with existing agents such as Claude Code, Codex and Hermes without requiring developers to rewrite them.

Sentry adds a separate hardware watchdog running on Nvidia’s BlueField-4 processors. Nvidia says it continuously monitors agent activity from outside the agent’s environment and can quarantine agents attempting to cross their boundaries within milliseconds.

The approach is designed for agents that work for hours or days, write code and interact with business systems. Instead of relying only on the model to follow instructions, the infrastructure limits which actions it can actually carry out.

Anthropic has collaborated with Nvidia to add protections to Claude Managed Agents, while SpaceXAI is using the platform for Cursor coding agents and Grok models. Salesforce has integrated OpenShell with Slack, and SAP is embedding it into Joule Studio.

Nvidia says more than 100 organizations are working with the technologies, including Microsoft, CrowdStrike, Cisco, Palo Alto Networks, Palantir and ServiceNow. The effort also extends to robotics, banks and energy infrastructure.

Jensen Huang: “Safety and security require full-stack engineering.”

OpenShell is broadly available, with platform software accessible through Nvidia’s developer resources and GitHub. Sentry is presented as a BlueField-4-based reference system design.

item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
US Treasuries are lagging equities by a historic margin:
S&P 500 futures have outperformed 10Y Treasury note futures by +23.3 percentage points over the last 6 months, the largest outperformance since 2021.
This also marks the 6th-largest underperformance of 10Y Note futures this century.
This comes as S&P 500 futures have risen +17.6% over this period, trading near their all-time high.
At the same time, 10Y Note futures have declined -5.7%, to their lowest level since June 2007.
To put this into perspective, 10Y Note futures outperformed S&P 500 futures by as much as +40.3 percentage points during the 6-month period in the 2008 Financial Crisis.
Stocks and Treasuries are diverging at a historic pace.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: US bond market volatility is at historic levels. The MOVE index jumped +19% last week, its largest...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
US bond market volatility is at historic levels.
The MOVE index jumped +19% last week, its largest weekly increase since April 2025, following "Liberation Day."
This index is also called the "VIX of bonds" and measures the yield volatility of 2Y, 5Y, 10Y, and 30Y Treasuries.
This marks its 3rd-largest weekly increase since the 2022 bear market.
The move comes as the 10Y Note Yield jumped +17 basis points last week, to 5.17%, its highest level since June 2007.
At the same time, the 30Y Note Yield rose +16 basis points and surpassed 5.50% for the first time since June 2004.
To put this into perspective, in the week ending March 17th, 2023, the MOVE Index surged +29% following the US banking crisis, when 3 regional banks collapsed.
The US Treasury market is experiencing crisis-like volatility.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: The Consumer Sentiment Index fell -3.6 points in September, to 48.1, its 2nd-lowest level...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: The Consumer Sentiment Index fell -3.6 points in September, to 48.1, its 2nd-lowest level in history.
This marks the 2nd consecutive monthly decline, totaling -7.1 points.
This comes as the Current Conditions Index decreased -1.0 point, to 50.9, its 4th-lowest reading on record.
At the same time, the Consumer Expectations Index dropped -5.2 points, to 46.3, its 2nd-lowest since 1980.
This year, the sentiment has deteriorated for all groups by age, education, geography, political party and income.
The decline has been driven by a higher cost-of-living, as higher fuel prices, persistent inflation, rising mortgage rates, and weaker purchasing power.
Consumer sentiment is at crisis levels.

Retail investors are locking in gains in tech.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Central banks are likely buying way more gold than official figures suggest: World central banks ac...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Central banks are likely buying way more gold than official figures suggest:
World central banks acquired +44 tonnes of gold in July, +158% above the pre-2022 average of +17 tonnes, according to Goldman Sachs.
This brings the 3-month average of purchases to +91 tonnes, near its highest since mid-2025.
By comparison, the 12-month moving average has oscillated between +50 and +60 tonnes over the last few months.
Meanwhile, official central bank purchases of gold stood at +23 tonnes in July, or 21 tonnes below actual levels.
Furthermore, official monthly purchases have not exceeded +60 tonnes in any month since November 2024, also representing a wide discrepancy.
Central bank gold demand may be much greater than official figures suggest.

item.title: @wallstengine: CHINA 🇨🇳 WEIGHS EASING RESTRICTIONS ON NEW $NVDA CHIP PURCHASES Beijing has signaled it may allow...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
CHINA 🇨🇳 WEIGHS EASING RESTRICTIONS ON NEW $NVDA CHIP PURCHASES
Beijing has signaled it may allow Alibaba, ByteDance and others to buy Nvidia’s new RTX Pro 5500, per The Information.
ByteDance alone is weighing an order for about 1M chips.
Key details:
• Nvidia plans to begin shipments in late December • Targeting ~500K chips per quarter for China • ByteDance’s potential order alone could take 2 quarters to fill • Buyers plan to put 8 chips per server to run AI models • Price: ~85K-90K yuan, roughly $13K each • Similar pricing to Huawei’s Ascend 950PR
The RTX Pro 5500 is not one of Nvidia’s top data-center AI chips and lacks the high-speed interconnects and premium memory used in those systems.
The bigger story is China’s compute shortage. AI companies are rolling out products faster than domestic chip supply can keep up, with Huawei itself recently saying it cannot meet demand.
Approval timing, quantities and conditions are still unclear.
item.content:encoded:
CHINA 🇨🇳 WEIGHS EASING RESTRICTIONS ON NEW $NVDA CHIP PURCHASES

Beijing has signaled it may allow Alibaba, ByteDance and others to buy Nvidia’s new RTX Pro 5500, per The Information.

ByteDance alone is weighing an order for about 1M chips.

Key details:

• Nvidia plans to begin shipments in late December
• Targeting ~500K chips per quarter for China
• ByteDance’s potential order alone could take 2 quarters to fill
• Buyers plan to put 8 chips per server to run AI models

• Similar pricing to Huawei’s Ascend 950PR

The RTX Pro 5500 is not one of Nvidia’s top data-center AI chips and lacks the high-speed interconnects and premium memory used in those systems.

The bigger story is China’s compute shortage. AI companies are rolling out products faster than domestic chip supply can keep up, with Huawei itself recently saying it cannot meet demand.

Approval timing, quantities and conditions are still unclear.

This proportion now stands ~6 percentage points above the 2000 Dot-Com Bubble peak.
Foreign appetite for US equities is historically strong.

item.description:

Higher for longer is creating meaningful income opportunities.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: Global debt jumped by more than +$10 trillion in H1 2026, to a record $365 trillion. Emer...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Global debt jumped by more than +$10 trillion in H1 2026, to a record $365 trillion.
Emerging-market debt drove the increase, rising +$6.5 trillion, to a record $110 trillion, with most of the surge coming from governments and non-financial companies.
Excluding China, emerging-market and developing-economy debt soared to a record $38 trillion.
Global debt now stands at ~310% of global GDP, although the ratio has fallen -25 percentage points from its early-2021 peak, largely because inflation has boosted nominal GDP rather than because of deleveraging.
Meanwhile, developed economies paid more than $3.3 trillion in interest on marketable government debt over the last year, exceeding estimated global spending on AI at $2.6 trillion, defense at $3.1 trillion, and clean energy at $2.3 trillion.
This comes as annual government interest payments across the G7 alone surged +85% YoY.
The global debt crisis is in uncharted territory.

item.title: @WatcherGuru: Timeline of events since Congress failed to pass the Crypto Clarity Act September 17: • SEC allows...
item.dc:creator: @WatcherGuru
item.description:
Timeline of events since Congress failed to pass the Crypto Clarity Act
September 17: • SEC allows limited on-chain trading of tokenized US stocks. • CFTC allows developers to build passive derivatives software without registering as brokers, including for crypto markets. • SEC Chair Atkins says tokenization rules are moving toward a longer-term framework.
September 18: • CFTC files new crypto market rules, moving them into White House review.
September 23: • CFTC Chair Selig says the agency is establishing clear crypto market structure rules. • CFTC outlines plans for 24/7 on-chain, tokenized financial markets. • Trump administration considers promoting dollar-backed stablecoins internationally.
September 24: • CFTC issues updated guidance on tokenized assets and blockchain recordkeeping. • Federal Reserve proposes rules for stablecoin issuers under the GENIUS Act.
September 25: • SEC staff releases new guidance on how securities laws apply to crypto. • SEC Commissioner calls to end mass collection of sensitive KYC data.
item.content:encoded:
Timeline of events since Congress failed to pass the Crypto Clarity Act

September 17:
• SEC allows limited on-chain trading of tokenized US stocks.
• CFTC allows developers to build passive derivatives software without registering as brokers, including for crypto markets.
• SEC Chair Atkins says tokenization rules are moving toward a longer-term framework.

September 18:
• CFTC files new crypto market rules, moving them into White House review.

September 23:
• CFTC Chair Selig says the agency is establishing clear crypto market structure rules.
• CFTC outlines plans for 24/7 on-chain, tokenized financial markets.
• Trump administration considers promoting dollar-backed stablecoins internationally.

September 24:
• CFTC issues updated guidance on tokenized assets and blockchain recordkeeping.
• Federal Reserve proposes rules for stablecoin issuers under the GENIUS Act.

September 25:
• SEC staff releases new guidance on how securities laws apply to crypto.
• SEC Commissioner calls to end mass collection of sensitive KYC data.

item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: The US and China have reached a trade deal to lower tariffs on $30 billion worth of "non-sensitive goods" after President Trump and President Xi met this week.
This deal will likely lower prices on a variety of consumer goods, including small appliances, toys, holiday decorations, and kids' car seats.
In return, China will cut tariffs on agricultural goods and seafood, wood products, cosmetics, and medical devices.
China has also agreed to import 10 million metric tons of US coal in 2027 and 2028.
Rare earths are still being discussed, the White House said.

item.description:
The U.S. 🇺🇸 and China 🇨🇳 agreed to recommend more favorable tariff treatment on $30B of non-sensitive goods in each direction following Xi Jinping’s state visit.
U.S. exports covered include agriculture, seafood, wood products, cosmetics and medical devices, while U.S. imports include toys, small appliances and other consumer goods.
China also agreed to buy at least 10M metric tons of U.S. coal in both 2027 and 2028. The tariff changes are recommendations for now and are not yet in force.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Global oil markets are facing a historic loss of diesel supply: Diesel supply from the Middle East...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Global oil markets are facing a historic loss of diesel supply:
Diesel supply from the Middle East dropped by -835,000 barrels per day on average between March and August 2026 compared to the same period in 2025, according to Vortexa estimates.
At the same time, Russian diesel supply fell -377,000 barrels per day.
Meanwhile, Kpler estimates diesel supply was down -750,000 barrels per day in the Middle East over the same period and -361,000 barrels per day in Russia, while Energy Aspects estimates declines of -733,000 and -307,000 barrels per day, respectively.
This puts the average estimated diesel supply loss at -772,667 barrels per day in the Middle East and -348,333 barrels per day in Russia, or -1.1 million combined.
Furthermore, Russian diesel supply plunged -615,000 barrels per day YoY on average in July and August, following Russia's diesel-export ban.
The global diesel market crisis is deepening.
item.content:encoded:
Global oil markets are facing a historic loss of diesel supply:

Diesel supply from the Middle East dropped by -835,000 barrels per day on average between March and August 2026 compared to the same period in 2025, according to Vortexa estimates.

At the same time, Russian diesel supply fell -377,000 barrels per day.

Meanwhile, Kpler estimates diesel supply was down -750,000 barrels per day in the Middle East over the same period and -361,000 barrels per day in Russia, while Energy Aspects estimates declines of -733,000 and -307,000 barrels per day, respectively.

This puts the average estimated diesel supply loss at -772,667 barrels per day in the Middle East and -348,333 barrels per day in Russia, or -1.1 million combined.

Furthermore, Russian diesel supply plunged -615,000 barrels per day YoY on average in July and August, following Russia's diesel-export ban.

The global diesel market crisis is deepening.
